cards.title: Lifetime owners close before replacement
items: Service cancellation joins discovery, native event draining and accepted mutations before Store.Close.
Library move, sync, restore and Undo stop and join the applicable Service before changing storage; relocated libraries reopen with a fresh owner.
Pending configuration commands cancel both an existing scan and any scan registered before command acceptance. No mutex spans the blocking send.

cards.title: The state owner binds the pair
items: Queue mutation, watch observation, handoff linking and companion capture share the short state owner. A snapshot cannot split a successful publication.
Ordinary collection History excludes mutable watch and intake journals. Explicit restore and Undo enroll and validate both images before replacement.
Missing images remain explicitly absent. Interrupted replacement retains recovery evidence instead of presenting a partial pair as healthy.

cards.title: Authority is native, not portable
items: A committed fence precedes the first live image replacement. Restore, Undo and restored absence require explicit watch activation.
The authority clock and lifetime coordination are excluded from snapshots and ordinary History. Library moves retain authority; sync destinations keep their own.
First enrollment publishes only a fully initialized, committed, closed SQLite file with native no-replace semantics. A published generation is never deleted or reused after a flush failure.

cards.title: Borrowed file ownership does not rebind the queue
items: Completed hash-verified staging can retry without reopening the original source. Otherwise selection happens after staging ownership is released.

After staging ownership is reacquired, the reservation is revalidated. State-owned checks before selection and at final completion protect the queue attempt; native identity, size and modification time bind the selected descriptor around copy.
After staging releases ownership, final state-owned authorization rejects revocation during copying before publishing a ready queue receipt.

cards.title: Native registrations have their own lifetime
items: Each native directory identity has one selected registration path. Same-path identity replacement requires a fresh backend.

A successor drains events before installing its complete registration set, then rechecks directory identity, native registrations and cancellation before publication. Failed construction closes the candidate and retains the previous owner.
Closing a registration owner preserves the backend Close error, cancels its child drain and joins that drain before returning.

Source evidence: 05102c1cc0c4b1db00826dc007753b544162e79b; internal/intake/watch_events.go:23–140; internal/intake/watch_service.go:159–171,206–256,274–295. These ranges cover registration identity, complete successor installation and postvalidation, immediate follow-up scanning, and drain cancellation/join. Native-platform qualification is separate.
